item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q002_mazg_hise_remote_homology","answer":"SCOPe 2.08 supports remote homology—probable common ancestry—between d1vmga_ and d1y6xa1. They belong to different families: MazG-like (a.204.1.2; SUNID 116993) and HisE-like (PRA-PH; a.204.1.4; SUNID 140797), respectively, within the same all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases superfamily (a.204.1; SUNID 101386). The superfamily explicitly implies homology. Their shared fold (a.204) and all-alpha class (a) describe structural similarity; those levels alone would not establish common ancestry. SCOPe describes a shared active-site module comprising five helices, four contributed by one subunit or structural repeat and one by another.\n\nThis supports an ancestral catalytic architecture, not identical biochemical specificity or close orthology. d1vmga_ is classified as a hypothetical Sulfolobus solfataricus protein, whereas d1y6xa1 is the A:7–93 domain of Mycobacterium tuberculosis phosphoribosyl-ATP pyrophosphatase HisE. It would exceed this evidence to assign HisE's specific reaction or histidine-biosynthesis role to d1vmga_, or to assign MazG-like substrate breadth or physiological roles to d1y6xa1. Identical substrates, catalytic residues, metal requirements, kinetics, or oligomeric arrangements are not established by superfamily membership. Such transfers require independent sequence and active-site comparisons, ligand/metal and assembly evidence, and biochemical substrate-specificity measurements; physiological roles additionally require biological context. Either structure may inform a conserved-core comparison, but detailed active-site modeling requires a validated alignment and compatible domain and assembly context.","evidence_used":["Pretrained knowledge of SCOPe hierarchy and limits of functional transfer","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains","mcp__scope__get_scop_node","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1vmga_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1vmga_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1y6xa1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1y6xa1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101386","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101386/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101386/homology"]}]}
